comparisons.peer_topic: Derivative Instrument Presentation and Netting Adjustments
comparisons.peer_summary: The table presents derivative assets and liabilities on a gross basis prior to netting, which are then adjusted to reflect counterparty and cash collateral netting effects from legally enforceable master netting agreements.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Bank of America (BAC) discuss the presentation of derivative assets and liabilities on a gross basis prior to the application of counterparty and cash collateral netting. GS specifically details the hypothetical impact of electing to settle transactions with an EMEA clearing organization on a daily basis, which would have reduced gross derivative assets by $64.19 billion and liabilities by $62.86 billion as of December 2023. BAC similarly presents derivative balances on a gross basis, adjusted for counterparty and cash collateral netting effects from legally enforceable master netting agreements, but does not disclose a specific election or quantitative impact for a regional clearing settlement election like GS.

sentences.text: • During 2024, as permitted under the rules of a clearing organization in Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA), the firm elected to settle its transactions with this clearing organization on a daily basis. The impact of reflecting transactions with this clearing organization as settled would have been a reduction in gross derivative assets of $64.19 billion and a reduction in gross derivative liabilities of $62.86 billion as of December 2023, and a corresponding decrease in counterparty and cash collateral netting, with no impact to the consolidated balance sheets.
Balances are presented on a gross basis, prior to the application of counterparty and cash collateral netting.

Total gross derivative assets and liabilities are adjusted on an aggregate basis to take into consideration the effects of legally enforceable master netting agreements, which include reducing the balance for counterparty netting and cash collateral received or paid.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company's derivative mark-to-market receivables and payables include significant netting against OTC, cleared, and exchange-traded derivatives, with approximately $264 billion, $36 billion, and $35 billion attributed to each respectively for 2024. Substantially all netting of cash collateral received and paid is against OTC derivative assets and liabilities, while $13 billion of assets and $15 billion of liabilities remain not subject to enforceable master netting agreements.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citigroup (C) disclose the impact of netting and clearing arrangements on derivative balances. GS explicitly quantifies the reduction in gross derivative assets ($64.19 billion) and liabilities ($62.86 billion) that would result from settling with an EMEA clearing organization on a daily basis. C provides a breakdown of netting amounts by derivative type (OTC, cleared, exchange-traded), totaling $264 billion, $36 billion, and $35 billion respectively, and notes that substantially all cash collateral netting is against OTC derivatives. While both address the mechanics and volume of netting/clearing, GS focuses on a specific election's balance sheet impact, whereas C focuses on the composition of netting across different derivative categories.

comparisons.peer_topic: Netting Policy for Derivatives and Cash Collateral
comparisons.peer_summary: As permitted under U.S. GAAP, the firm nets derivative receivables and payables with related cash collateral receivables and payables when a legally enforceable master netting agreement exists.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) discuss accounting policies related to netting and collateral. GS describes an election to settle with an EMEA clearing organization on a daily basis, impacting gross derivative asset/liability presentation. JPM discloses its election, as permitted under U.S. GAAP, to net derivative receivables/payables with related cash collateral when a legally enforceable master netting agreement exists. Both disclosures relate to the application of netting and collateral in derivative accounting, but GS highlights a specific regional clearing mechanism's impact, while JPM describes a general U.S. GAAP election for collateral netting.
